Databricks discusses funding round at $225 billion valuation — Channel NewsAsia
Fedir Kryshtovskyi
21

01:49
Databricks, a developer of software for working with data and artificial intelligence, is holding preliminary talks to raise several billion dollars. The new funding round could value the company at about $225 billion, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
Deal terms may change
As Channel NewsAsia reports , The Wall Street Journal published this information on November 20. The talks are ongoing, and the terms of the potential deal may still change. Databricks did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram .
Previous round and products
In August, Databricks said it had raised $5 billion at a valuation of $190 billion. The company was founded in 2013; it develops software products for storing, managing and analyzing data, as well as for building artificial intelligence applications.
Databricks competes with Snowflake, and the company is considered a candidate for a future stock market listing. Databricks previously said that the annual revenue run rate of its Lakebase product exceeded $100 million, while the figure for its Lakehouse data warehousing business reached more than $1.5 billion.

candidates.title: Oracle OpenAI Contract Fully Funded After $20B Raise
candidates.snippet: Oracle OpenAI Contract Fully Funded After $20B Raise shattered.io
candidates.text:
Home

Oracle Says OpenAI Deal Is Funded After $20B Raise
Priya Anand
Updated Nov 22, 2026 · 16 min read
Photo: Peter Kaminski from San Francisco, California, USA, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
Oracle told investors on November 20, 2026 that it has locked down the money for its OpenAI infrastructure contract. In the company’s own words, “Oracle has secured all the funding we need to fulfill our contract with OpenAI.” The statement landed after a final capital raise earlier in November, and it aims to settle a question that has hung over the Oracle OpenAI contract for months: who pays for the servers, the buildings and the power?
Table of Contents
What Oracle Actually Said on November 20
The $20 Billion Raise: $10 Billion in Stock, $10 Billion in Debt
What the Securities Filing Says and Leaves Out
Closing date: November 4, 2026
Use of proceeds: general corporate purposes
Vendor Financing and the Investor Day Plan
Why “Fully Funded” Does Not Mean Fully Paid For
The Unknown: What the OpenAI Contract Is Worth
What Oracle Said, in Its Own Words
How Oracle’s Funding Claim Compares With Other AI Spenders
Historical Context: Cloud Buildouts and the Cost of Capacity
Market Impact: Investors, Lenders and Suppliers
Why This Matters for the AI Models Race
What Could Still Go Wrong
Five Predictions for the Next Two Quarters
Frequently Asked Questions
What did Oracle announce about its OpenAI contract?
How much did Oracle raise?
Is the $20 billion reserved for OpenAI?
How much is the OpenAI contract worth?
What is vendor financing?
Is Oracle really the first fully funded hyperscaler?
Does the funding guarantee OpenAI will get its capacity on time?
Related
The raise totaled $20 billion, split roughly evenly between $10 billion in stock and $10 billion in debt. Oracle also called itself the first hyperscaler fully funded for this investment cycle. That is a bold claim in a year when capital markets have been testing every AI spender, including Anthropic, which priced its IPO at $83 and raised $81.31 billion according to our earlier coverage.
This analysis separates what Oracle confirmed from what it did not. The company gave two headline numbers, one date and a handful of carefully worded sentences. It did not give the contract’s total value, its length or its payment schedule. Those gaps matter as much as the confirmed facts, and we treat them that way throughout.

What Oracle Actually Said on November 20
Oracle’s message came in a few short statements, and each one does a specific job. The first states the conclusion: the money needed for the OpenAI contract is secured. The second explains how Oracle got there, pointing to a final capital raise earlier in the month. The third tries to head off a different worry, that Oracle still needs extra help from suppliers to finish the job.
On that third point, Oracle said any further private discussions with vendors are just additional options. It added that its ability to deliver on the OpenAI contract does not depend on those discussions. Read together, the statements frame vendor talks as optional upside rather than a missing piece of the plan.

Indian Startups Raise $31.3M; A2B’s $180M Deal Stands Out
OpenAI Cuts Funding Target $10B to $20B [2026]
Microsoft Winds Down Oracle AI Cloud Deal From 2023 [2026]
Several outlets carried the news, including Reuters, The Indian Express, TechStory and The Information, according to the story’s tracking across named publications. The wording across those reports matches the company’s own language, which suggests the claim comes from a single Oracle statement rather than from independent verification of the funding. That distinction shapes how much weight readers should put on the word “fully.”
The $20 Billion Raise: $10 Billion in Stock, $10 Billion in Debt
The final raise worked out to about $20 billion. Roughly $10 billion came from selling new stock, and roughly $10 billion came from borrowing. Oracle’s securities filing says both offerings closed on November 4, 2026. That date matters because it places the money in Oracle’s accounts weeks before the public announcement, so the funding claim rests on completed transactions rather than on a pipeline of deals still in progress.
A 50/50 mix of equity and debt is a deliberate balance. Stock dilutes existing shareholders but adds no interest burden. Debt avoids dilution but adds fixed payments that must be met whether or not AI demand shows up on schedule. By splitting the raise evenly, Oracle limited how much it leans on either lever. Rating agencies and lenders tend to reward that kind of balance, though Oracle has not published any rating changes in the sources we reviewed.
The $20 billion is also the “final” raise in Oracle’s framing, which implies Oracle does not expect to return for another large round to cover this contract. Oracle did not state that as a promise, but investors will likely read it that way. If a new offering appears soon, the “fully funded” language will look premature.

The post Lockheed Martin Receives $2.35 Billion In Direct Defense Awards Across F-35, C-5 And Trident Programs appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Lockheed Martin Receives $2.35 Billion In Direct Defense Awards Across F-35, C-5 And Trident Programs
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 3:49 PM
Lockheed Martin Receives $2.35 Billion In Direct Defense Awards Across F-35, C-5 And Trident Programs
Lockheed Martin received five directly valued defense awards totaling approximately $2.35 billion, along with positions on two large multiple-award contract vehicles whose shared ceilings cannot be assigned to any individual contractor.
The largest direct award is a Navy letter-contract modification valued at up to $1.53 billion for Trident II D5 missile production and deployed-systems support. The sole-source effort will continue through September 2031.
Aircraft Production And Sustainment
The company received a $330.6 million modification for long-lead materials supporting 75 Lot 22 F-35 aircraft. The full amount was obligated at award, with work continuing through December 2030.
A separate $93.2 million order covers F-35 depot test equipment, cybersecurity upgrades, repair capacity, technical data, and engineering support. The Navy, Air Force, and cooperative-program partners obligated the complete order value.
The Air Force also awarded Lockheed Martin a $316.6 million C-5 Galaxy logistics-support contract. Approximately $23.7 million was initially obligated for supply-chain, repair, engineering, and technical services.
A $72.6 million F-35 Block 4 modification increases the ceiling for software, cybersecurity, and program-management work, but no funding was obligated at award.
Lockheed Martin was additionally selected for the Navy’s shared $7.13 billion Surface Electronic Warfare Improvement Program vehicle and the Air Force’s $16.1 billion Advanced Propulsion Enterprise vehicle. Those ceilings represent pools available to all selected contractors and are not included in Lockheed Martin’s $2.35 billion direct-award total.

Want to keep track of the largest startup funding deals in 2026 with our curated list of $100 million-plus venture deals to U.S.-based companies? Check out The Crunchbase Megadeals Board .
This is a weekly feature that runs down the week’s Top 10 announced funding rounds in the U.S. Check out last week’s biggest funding deal roundup here .
It was a big week for tech startup exits, headlined by Anthropic pulling off its massive IPO. On the down side, however, tech stocks took a huge dive in the past few days. Should that negative sentiment and downward pressure persist, we can expect it to spill over into private markets.
For this past week, however, U.S. startups continued to secure sizable rounds, led by brain-computer interface company Science landing a fresh $400 million. Another seven American companies announced venture or growth funding of $100 million or more, and across the Atlantic, UK-based AI biotech startup Isomorphic Labs landed $5 billion, the largest financing of the week.
1. Science , $400M, neurotech : Science, a startup focused on brain-computer interface technology, and neural engineering, secured $400 million in Series D funding. The round brings total funding to date for the Alameda, California-based company to more than $900 million.
2. Model ML , $250M, AI and fintech : Model ML, an AI platform for financial and professional services, closed on $250 million in Series B funding at a $1.5 billion valuation. General Atlantic and QED Investors led the round for the three-year-old company, which is based in New York and London.
3. Galvanize Therapeutics , $130M, biotech : Redwood City, California-based Galvanize Therapeutics, a developer of pulsed electric field ablation technologies for oncology and chronic disease, picked up $130 million in Series D funding led by HealthQuest Capital .
4. General Flash , $128M, critical metals : General Flash, a developer of a new method to produce critical metals, announced that it has raised $128 million across seed and Series A rounds from a long list of investors.
5. Ramon.Space , $124M, space tech : Denver-based Ramon.Space, a developer of space computing infrastructure, pulled in $124M in Series B funding led by PSG .
6. Marrow Therapeutics , $120M, biotech : Watertown, Massachusetts-based Marrow Therapeutics, a developer of bone marrow-targeted therapies to treat severe blood disorders, announced its launch with a combined $173 million in Series A and B funding. Orbimed led its $120 million Series B round while Scion Life Sciences and venBio led the $53 million Series A.
7. Noeri , $110M, enterprise AI : Noeri, a developer of self-improving AI for enterprises and researchers, launched with $110 million in initial funding. Menlo Ventures led the round for the Palo Alto-based startup, which was founded by Stanford University computer science professors.
8. Seawolf Therapeutics , $100M, biotech : San Diego-based Seawolf Therapeutics, a biotech startup developing a novel DNA delivery platform, emerged from stealth and announced that it has raised $100 million in funding to date, with Versant Ventures , MPM BioImpact and Novartis Venture Fund as lead investors.
9. BrightAI , $97M, physical AI : BrightAI, a startup developing a sensor, drone and robotics-driven platform to bring continuous observability to infrastructure-heavy industries like power, water, and energy, secured $97 million in new funding. Smith Point Capital led the financing for the Silicon Valley-based company.
10. Vincue , $93M, vehicle intelligence platform : Kansas City-based Vincue, developer of a vehicle lifecycle intelligence platform, closed on $93 million in growth capital led by Wavecrest Growth Partners .
And overseas:
Isomorphic Labs , $5B, AI and biotech : London-based Isomorphic Labs, a startup that applies AI to drug discovery, secured $5 billion in Series C funding. Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital led the financing for the five-year-old company, which also has offices in Massachusetts and Switzerland.
Methodology
We tracked the largest announced rounds in the Crunchbase database that were raised by U.S.-based companies for the period of Nov. 14-20, 2026. Although most announced rounds are in the database, there may be a small time lag, as some rounds are reported late in the week.

candidates.title: Doosan Raises $340 Million to Expand CCL Capacity Amid AI Data Center Boom
candidates.snippet: Doosan Raises $340 Million to Expand CCL Capacity Amid AI Data Center Boom Seoul Economic Daily
candidates.text:
Doosan Raises $340 Million to Expand CCL Capacity Amid AI Data Center Boom
Funds From National Growth Fund to Expand Jeungpyeong, Gimcheon Plants
CCL Plant Utilization Already Above 100%
New Production Lines and R&D Center Planned
Semiconductor Value Chain From Materials to Back-End Nears Completion
Market Signal |
Published 2026.11.22. 20:13:03 |
By Kim Byung-joon econ_jun@sedaily.com
| Summary | Save
A A A
This article appeared on Signal, the capital markets compass, at 2:13 p.m. on Nov. 22, 2026.
View of Doosan's headquarters in Seongnam, Gyeonggi Province. Doosan
Doosan (000150) is raising 500 billion won ($340 million) from the National Growth Fund to expand its copper clad laminate (CCL) production plants, responding to a surge in demand for high-value CCL driven by expanding investment in artificial intelligence data centers. Analysts say Doosan Group is completing a semiconductor value chain that now spans semiconductor materials, wafers — the discs on which chips are built — through its acquisition of SK Siltron, and back-end processing at Doosan Tesna.
Doosan's domestic CCL production lines are already running above 100% utilization, leaving the company in need of added capacity through expansion, according to investment banking sources on the 22nd. "The company will raise funds from the National Growth Fund and the Korea Development Bank and invest in domestic plants, excluding China," one investment banking source said.
This is not Doosan's first expansion plan. The company previously announced it would invest 400 billion won by 2028 to build a CCL production facility for optical modules spanning about 33,000 square meters next to its flexible copper clad laminate (FCCL) plant in Gimje, Jeonbuk State. Adding the expansion of the Jeungpyeong plant through low-interest loans from the National Growth Fund is seen as a move to respond quickly to rapidly rising CCL demand. Unlike Gimje, which requires new construction, the Jeungpyeong and Gimcheon expansions can be completed relatively quickly.
Demand for CCL used in optical modules is surging as AI data centers proliferate and networks shift to ultra-high speeds of 800G and above. Optical modules convert electrical signals between servers and network equipment into light signals, and CCL is a core material for printed circuit boards. Securities analysts said rising demand for optical module CCL is creating a seller's market. "With a CCL supply shortage expected to persist for the next two to three years, suppliers are likely to secure favorable pricing terms when signing long-term supply contracts," said Kim Min-kyung, an analyst at Hana Securities.
Doosan also plans to build a research and development center in Yongin, Gyeonggi Province. Doosan Group had initially planned to build an advanced technology R&D center focused on hydrogen research involving Doosan Enerbility, Doosan Fuel Cell and Doosan Mobility Innovation, but it is now expected to extend the center's scope to semiconductor R&D. The move aims to upgrade and strengthen technological competitiveness as the group completes its semiconductor value chain. Under the structure, SK Siltron produces wafers, the starting point of chip manufacturing, Doosan supplies CCL, and Doosan Tesna handles back-end processes such as wafer testing and package testing for system semiconductors. The Korea Development Bank, together with Woori Bank, earlier arranged 2.5 trillion won in acquisition financing for the SK Siltron purchase.
Funding from the National Growth Fund is confirmed after a review of eligibility criteria including business viability, technology and creditworthiness, followed by deliberation and approval by an investment review committee and a fund management committee. Doosan has cleared the business viability and creditworthiness stages ahead of the investment review committee, meaning the loan process is effectively in its final phase. "The Korea Development Bank's support of low-interest loans for both Doosan's SK Siltron acquisition and its plant expansion reads as a show of commitment to fostering the advanced semiconductor industry," another investment banking source said.
The National Growth Fund provides low-interest loans to advanced strategic industries and their ecosystems, including AI, semiconductors, secondary batteries, biotechnology and energy infrastructure. It has previously extended low-interest loans of 2.5 trillion won to Samsung Electronics' (005930) fifth production line in Pyeongtaek, 1.5 trillion won to LG Display (034220) and 750 billion won to the Sinan Ui offshore wind power project. It also provided 300 billion won to SK Bioscience (302440) to secure production facilities and made a 250 billion won direct investment in Rebellions.
Beyond Doosan, domestic materials, parts and equipment companies are also expanding investment. Kolon Industries (120110) has added production lines for modified polyphenylene oxide (mPPO), a low-dielectric material that reduces electrical signal loss in semiconductor circuit boards, in response to growth in the AI and semiconductor industries. LG Chem (051910) is also investing in CCL, aiming to broaden its applications from memory chips to non-memory areas such as system-in-package (SiP).

candidates.title: Raytheon Receives $159.4 Million In Direct Navy Awards For Missile And Sensor Systems
candidates.snippet:
Raytheon received three directly valued Navy awards totaling approximately $159.4 million for Rolling Airframe Missile and Cooperative Engagement Capability work.
The post Raytheon Receives $159.4 Million In Direct Navy Awards For Missile And Sensor Systems appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Raytheon Receives $159.4 Million In Direct Navy Awards For Missile And Sensor Systems
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 3:42 PM
Raytheon Receives $159.4 Million In Direct Navy Awards For Missile And Sensor Systems
Raytheon received three directly valued Navy awards totaling approximately $159.4 million for Rolling Airframe Missile and Cooperative Engagement Capability work.
The largest award is a $120.3 million firm-fixed-price modification covering production of Rolling Airframe Missile Block 2B guided-missile round packs.
Missile Production And Engineering
The Block 2B modification supports Navy production and a Foreign Military Sales requirement for Japan. The Navy obligated $105.6 million, while Japan provided $14.7 million. Work will take place in Germany, Arizona, West Virginia, Great Britain, Ohio, and other U.S. locations through February 2030.
Raytheon also received a $12.3 million modification for design-agent and engineering support for the Rolling Airframe Missile system. Germany funded the complete award, which includes systems engineering, software maintenance, reliability, quality-assurance, logistics, and technical support through September 2028.
A separate $26.7 million modification supports the Cooperative Engagement Capability weapon system. The work includes design, development, integration, testing, and maintenance for the United States, Australia, Japan, and Canada. The full amount was obligated at award.
Raytheon was also named to the Navy’s shared $7.13 billion Surface Electronic Warfare Improvement Program contract and parent company RTX was selected for the Air Force’s $16.1 billion propulsion vehicle. Neither shared ceiling is included in Raytheon’s direct-award total because future task orders will determine actual revenue.

Венчурные сделки
На этой неделе было 11 раундов из этой категории, включая:
$110 млн — Variational. Децентрализованный протокол закрыл раунд серии B под руководством Bain Capital Crypto при участии Dragonfly, HSG, Peak XV Partners и 50T Funds. Оценка компании достигла $1,5 млрд. Пользователи могут торговать деривативами на криптоактивы, акции, индексы, сырьевые товары и валюты. Средства направят на увеличение числа доступных рынков и повышение лимитов открытого интереса на платформе Omni.
$30 млн — Nomad. Бразильский финтех-стартап привлек средства в рамках раунда серии C под руководством Tether Capital при участии Endeavor, Globo Ventures, Tiger Global Management и Spark Capital. Платформа предоставляет доступ к долларовым счетам, международным платежам и инвестиционным инструментам. Капитал направят на разработку продуктов на базе ИИ, расширение инвестиционной платформы и развитие инфраструктуры трансграничных расчетов.
$30 млн — Codex. Разработчик платежной инфраструктуры завершил раунд серии A под руководством Pantera Capital при участии Dragonfly Capital, Coinbase Ventures, TENET, Reciprocal Ventures, Fin Capital и LeadBlock Partners. Сервис обеспечивает конвертацию фиатных валют и стейблкоинов по институциональным курсам. Финансирование позволит масштабировать систему международных расчетов.
$25 млн — Avenia (ранее BRLA Digital). Бразильская финтех-компания завершила расширенный раунд серии A под руководством Lightspeed Faction при участии Flourish Ventures, Quona Capital, Big Bets, Headline Asia, Fluent Ventures, Tomorrow Capital и Patria Investments. Компания специализируется на трансграничных расчетах. Она также выпускает стейблкоин BRLA, привязанный к местной валюте. Средства направят на запуск новых продуктов и приобретение лицензированных финансовых организаций.
$10 млн — MetaComp. Платежный сервис привлек финансирование в рамках расширенного раунда Pre-Series A+ при участии Tether и Further Asset Management. Компания обслуживает трансграничные переводы в фиатных валютах и стейблкоинах. Капитал направят на лицензирование, обеспечение соответствия регуляторным требованиям и расширение сети расчетов между Азией, Ближним Востоком и Африкой.
$4 млн — TheHUB. Разработчик инфраструктурных решений провел посевной раунд под руководством Valor Capital Group при участии Adderall Capital, Keyrock, Staking Facilities и бизнес-ангелов. Компания создает сети с низкой задержкой для криптобирж, маркетмейкеров и валидаторов. Средства направят на расширение инженерной команды и выход на новые рынки.
$3,5 млн — End Close. Стартап завершил посевной раунд при участии Foundation Capital, Y Combinator, Liquid 2 Ventures, Sunflower Capital и Angel Invest. Команда разрабатывает инструменты автоматизированной сверки финансовых транзакций с использованием ИИ. Капитал направят на расширение штата разработчиков, коммерческого подразделения и подразделения по внедрению продукта.
$2,5 млн — LART. Стартап привлек финансирование в рамках посевного раунда при участии IBC Group, X21 Digital, Genesis Capital, Gaea Ventures и частных инвесторов. Протокол специализируется на токенизации произведений искусства и подтверждении их происхождения посредством блокчейна. Amentum Receives $38.3 Million In Aviation Awards And Positions On Two Major Contract Vehicles
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 4:23 PM
Amentum Receives $38.3 Million In Aviation Awards And Positions On Two Major Contract Vehicles
Amentum Services received two Army aviation-maintenance modifications totaling approximately $38.3 million and was selected for two major multiple-award contract vehicles.
The Army awarded an $18.4 million time-and-materials modification for worldwide aviation maintenance. The work includes level-of-effort support, pass-back maintenance, and aircraft modification installations.
Global Aviation Maintenance
The $18.4 million modification increased the cumulative value of contract W58RGZ-25-C-0003 to approximately $435.2 million. The full modification value was obligated using fiscal 2027 Army aircraft-procurement and operations-and-maintenance funding.
Amentum also received a $19.9 million modification under contract W58RGZ-25-C-0004. Work will be conducted at locations across Alaska, Arizona, California, Hawaii, Kansas, Montana, New Mexico, South Korea, Texas, and Washington through November 2027. The Army obligated the full amount.
These two modifications represent approximately $38.3 million in newly awarded, directly attributable value. The cumulative values of the underlying contracts are not added to that total because they include earlier awards.
Amentum was also selected for the Navy’s $7.13 billion Surface Electronic Warfare Improvement Program vehicle and the Air Force’s $16.1 billion Advanced Propulsion Enterprise contract. Those ceilings are shared with numerous companies and do not guarantee Amentum a specific amount. Actual value will depend on task orders competed and awarded under each vehicle.

candidates.title: University Of Michigan Library Receives More Than $21 Million For Culinary Archive
candidates.snippet:
The University of Michigan Library has received a bequest of more than $21 million from Daniel T. Longone to support the Janice Bluestein Longone Culinary Archive.
The post University Of Michigan Library Receives More Than $21 Million For Culinary Archive appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
University Of Michigan Library Receives More Than $21 Million For Culinary Archive
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 3:40 PM
University Of Michigan Library Receives More Than $21 Million For Culinary Archive
The University of Michigan Library has received a bequest of more than $21 million from Daniel T. Longone to support the Janice Bluestein Longone Culinary Archive.
The gift is the largest in the library’s history and honors Longone’s wife, Janice B. Longone, whose collecting and research helped establish the archive.
Preserving American Culinary History
The collection contains more than 30,000 cookbooks, recipes, restaurant menus, advertisements, and other materials documenting the history of food and drink in the United States.
Its holdings span the 18th through early 21st centuries, with particular strengths in community cookbooks, African American and immigrant cookbooks, handwritten recipes, restaurant menus, food advertising, wine, and viticulture.
One of its most significant items is the only known copy of Malinda Russell’s 1866 work, “A Domestic Cook Book,” the oldest known cookbook written by an African American woman.
Current collecting priorities include Native American cookbooks, regional cooking, immigrant foodways, vegetarian and vegan cuisine, and handwritten recipe collections.
Expanding Research And Public Access
The bequest will support preservation, acquisitions, cataloging, conservation, teaching, research, digitization, and public programming.
Funding will also support visiting scholars, research fellows, artists, seminars, workshops, curated digital collections, and an annual public lecture.
Longone previously contributed another $1.5 million to establish the Janice B. Longone Librarian for Culinary History. Juli McLoone, the archive’s longtime curator, holds the endowed position.
The library also plans to expand classroom access as students use the collection to investigate migration, identity, race, gender, labor, business, environmental issues, and everyday life.
KEY QUOTES:
This gift is an extraordinary investment in the future of an amazing culinary archive. The endowed librarian position provides dedicated leadership, and this level of support gives that leader the resources to preserve and build the collection, welcome and engage researchers and students, and connect its stories with the broader public. Together, these commitments ensure that Jan and Dan Longone’s vision will continue to flourish and impact scholars well into the future.
Lisa Carter, University Librarian And Dean Of Libraries At The University Of Michigan
She knew the value of looking at cookbooks unmitigated by a historian’s perspective.
Ruth Reichl, Chef And Food Writer
She would lead you down the rickety back stairs to her basement with all these dehumidifiers going and these metal racks full of books and you could spend as long as you wanted there. I thought I had struck gold.
Rick Bayless, Chef And Restaurateur

Kickstarter backers have pledged $15 million to the Flipper One, a pocket-sized Linux mini-computer that works with Wi-Fi and 5G networks. AI Illustration. Upload story photo >

The Flipper One, a pocket-sized mini-computer, has raised $15 million on Kickstarter, with $13 million coming in on the first day of the campaign. The device runs Linux and uses Wi-Fi and 5G rather than the RFID and NFC protocols of its predecessor, the Flipper Zero.
Why it matters
The campaign's rapid funding signals strong interest in a portable device aimed at networks, routers, and internet-connected hardware rather than only low-level wireless signals. Its focus on regular software and cellular connectivity distinguishes it from the earlier Flipper Zero, launched in 2020.
The Flipper One runs Linux, connects over Wi-Fi and 5G, supports eSIM for cellular networks, and can act as both a Wi-Fi client and hotspot. Its raw specifications such as processor and storage were not included in the reporting.
The players
Flipper Devices
Flipper Devices is the company behind the Flipper Zero and the Flipper One, known for pocket-sized hardware tools aimed at hobbyists and security researchers.
The details
The device is designed to interact with Wi-Fi networks, routers, and internet-connected devices, and once developers gain access, additional functionality is expected to emerge. Unlike the Flipper Zero, which works with Bluetooth, RFID, and NFC, the Flipper One relies on regular software and modern cellular technologies.
Timeline
2020: The predecessor Flipper Zero was launched.
November 21, 2026: Coverage of the Flipper One Kickstarter campaign was published.
The Tech Race
The Flipper One marks a departure from the Flipper Zero's focus on raw wireless protocols, moving toward general-purpose Linux computing and network-level tools. Its design reflects a broader trend of pocket hardware that bridges hobbyist experimentation and mainstream internet connectivity.
The device could give users a portable tool for working with Wi-Fi networks, routers, and cellular connections through regular Linux software. Backers and future buyers will be able to test network-connected devices without carrying a full laptop.
The takeaway
Portable hardware that runs standard software can open network experimentation to a wider audience than specialized single-purpose tools. Readers interested in the device should watch for developer documentation as access expands.

candidates.snippet: Insurtech Eight by Zero (8/0) raises $3 mn in seed funding led by Diagram Beinsure
candidates.text:
InsurTech News
Life Insurance News
🇨🇦 Canadian Insurance News
🇺🇸 US Insurance News
Eight by Zero targets insurance data integration costs
Canada Life invests in insurance interoperability platform
Munich Re Life US joins as reinsurance partner
Platform connects employee data across insurance products
Eight by Zero Technologies (8/0), a Montreal-based insurance technology company developing interoperability infrastructure, has raised $3 mn in seed funding to expand its data connectivity platform across the insurance industry.
The financing round was led by Diagram, with participation from Canada Life as a strategic investor.
Eight by Zero is also working with Munich Re Life US, a subsidiary of Munich Re Group, to address employee data integration challenges affecting group insurance and disability carriers.
Insurtech Eight by Zero has secured $3 mn in seed financing led by Diagram, with strategic participation from Canada Life.
The company’s interoperability platform connects insurers, third-party administrators, employers and HR systems, reducing the need for separately maintained data integrations.
Munich Re Life US is working with Eight by Zero to address employee data connectivity challenges for group and disability insurers, while the funding will support product development and expansion.
The new capital will support product development, expansion into additional insurance lines, customer implementation capacity and commercial growth.
Eight by Zero targets insurance data integration costs
Eight by Zero has developed a multi-tenant platform that connects insurers, third-party administrators (TPAs), employers and human resources systems through APIs and file-based integrations.
The technology replaces separate point-to-point connections with a shared connectivity layer designed to reduce repetitive integration work.
Insurance carriers frequently establish individual connections with employers to obtain employee information needed for underwriting, policy administration and claims-related processes. When several insurers provide different forms of coverage to the same employer, each may need to build and maintain its own integration.
Eight by Zero aims to eliminate that duplication by establishing a connection that can serve multiple insurance products and carriers.
Carriers have rebuilt the same integration for every employer they onboard. We build it once, and the carrier can get it for every line it writes for that employer. Disability and absence are where we’re proving it. The same employee data drives every other line of coverage, and that’s where we’re headed.
Sam Kasle, Co-Founder and CEO of Eight by Zero
The platform is already used by multiple insurance carriers across North America. Artificial intelligence supports initial integration setup and ongoing maintenance, while the underlying data mapping remains deterministic.
Canada Life invests in insurance interoperability platform
Canada Life participated in the seed round as a strategic investor, supporting Eight by Zero’s development of infrastructure intended to simplify information exchange between employers and insurance providers.
Julia McGillis, Executive Vice President, Workplace Benefits & Retirement at Canada Life, said the investment aligns with the insurer’s efforts to improve connectivity across benefits and insurance services.
“We see Eight by Zero as an opportunity to create a more connected experience for our plan sponsors and advisors,” McGillis said. She added that the platform’s capabilities would support Canada Life’s existing technology investments by reducing integration complexity for employers and insurance carriers.
Diagram, which led the financing, identified recurring integration costs as a significant operational burden for financial institutions.
Gaurav Kapoor, General Partner at Diagram, said insurers repeatedly devote technical resources to establishing employer connections that could otherwise be reused.
Inside any large financial institution, integration work quietly eats the roadmap, and insurers pay that cost again every time they onboard an employer.
Gaurav Kapoor, General Partner at Diagram
He said Eight by Zero had demonstrated its approach in disability and absence insurance, providing a basis for expansion into other coverage lines.
Munich Re Life US joins as reinsurance partner
Eight by Zero is working with Munich Re Life US to explore applications of its platform for group insurance and disability clients.
Employee data connectivity is particularly relevant to these insurers because changes in employment status, working hours or leave arrangements can affect coverage administration and claims handling.
Jinnah Cox, Vice President and Actuary, Group & Living Benefits at Munich Re Life US, described employee information exchange as a continuing operational challenge for the sector. The reinsurer expects its collaboration with Eight by Zero to help clients assess a connectivity solution that can support multiple insurance lines.
Platform connects employee data across insurance products
Eight by Zero’s initial applications focus on disability insurance and absence management, where timely employee information is needed to administer benefits and support policyholders.
Changes such as an employee taking medical leave, sustaining a workplace injury, reducing working hours or leaving an organization may need to be communicated to several insurance providers.
Disability insurers, workers’ compensation carriers, life insurers and employee benefits administrators can each require updated information about the same individual.
Under conventional arrangements, these organizations often receive the data through separately developed and maintained integrations.
Eight by Zero’s shared connectivity infrastructure is intended to make current employee information available across the relevant insurance products without requiring carriers to maintain individual connections for each coverage line.

Deutsche Telekom Pours Another Quarter-Billion Into Munich AI Site, Lands microagi as Tenant
Published on 11/22/2026 at 10:30 | Editorial boerse-global.de
Telekom plans to raise Munich AI factory capacity to 20 MW with under EUR 250 million more investment; microagi to train robotics models there.
Telekom, Pours, Another, Quarter-Billion, Into, Munich, Site, Lands, Tenant, EUR Illustration mit AI erstellt.
Deutsche Telekom is turning its Munich AI factory into a magnet for industrial robotics work while deepening its ties to the continent's most closely watched AI startup. The Bonn-based carrier said on 18 November that microagi will train its robotics models for industrial clients at the Munich site, keeping production data and manufacturing know-how in Germany and under the customers' own control.
The arrangement comes alongside a capacity upgrade: Telekom plans to lift the Munich facility's output to 20 megawatts, backed by just under a further EUR 250 million of investment. Additional NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra systems will form part of the expansion. The company is also weighing whether to extend its footprint in Bavaria beyond the announced buildout, though any such move remains subject to a final investment decision.
Sovereign AI Push Tied to Mistral Stake
Alongside the infrastructure work, Telekom is pursuing a strategic partnership with Mistral AI aimed at supplying German companies and public authorities with sovereign AI solutions. The first step in that tie-up is a EUR 100 million investment in Mistral AI by T.Capital Tech Fund, the group's venture arm, made as part of the startup's Series D financing round.
Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying Deutsche Telekom?
Separately, the group disclosed on 16 November that it had repurchased roughly 4.24 million of its own shares between 9 and 13 November. Since the current buyback programme began on 10 August, it had acquired around 53.6 million treasury shares by the end of that window.
Analysts Split on Valuation
Research houses are pulling in different directions on the stock. Barclays raised its price target to EUR 33 from EUR 32 on 11 November while reaffirming its "Overweight" rating. Kepler Cheuvreux moved the other way on 18 November, cutting its target to EUR 30 from EUR 32 and keeping a "Hold" stance. The shares added 0.5% on Friday to close at EUR 26.18.

The capital will be allocated to expanding the portfolio of proprietary models such as Flint Image and Lockstep, and to developing each::studio, a tool aimed at film and VFX teams that allows working with generative media without API integration. For professionals in the sector, this represents a more controlled and reusable AI generation pathway, with specialized models that reduce the cost of failed iterations and accelerate the creation of character and motion variants in audiovisual production.
One million generations a day and there are still those asking the render to hurry up ⏱️
Nearly one million daily generations for 750 organizations sounds like someone on the VFX team will no longer have an excuse to deliver the storyboard on Monday. That said, with each::studio promising to work without touching an API, more than one technician will discover that their new most in-demand skill will be explaining to the producer that the generate button doesn't make coffee.

Telangana tech startups raise $726 mn in 9M 2026; funding rounds dip 30%: Tracxn
According to Tracxn’s analysis, most of the fresh capital flowed into a handful of large early-stage funding rounds, led by data centre company CtrlS, as well as enterprise infrastructure businesses based in Hyderabad.

The deal alone accounted for 58 per cent of total funding and 80 per cent of the $527 million increase over 9M 2025. Telangana-based tech companies raised $726 million in funding during the first nine months of 2026 (9M 2026), marking a 266 per cent increase from $199 million in the year-ago period and a 12 per cent rise from $647 million in 9M 2024, according to a Tracxn report.
However, the number of funding rounds declined 30 per cent to 73 from 105 a year earlier, according to the Telangana Tech – 9M 2026 Report by Tracxn, which tracks funding, investors, exits, unicorns and city-level activity between January 1 and September 30, 2026.
Advt
According to the report, most of the fresh capital flowed into a handful of large early-stage funding rounds, led by data centre company CtrlS , as well as enterprise infrastructure businesses based in Hyderabad.
However, deal activity declined, with both seed- and early-stage funding rounds falling from the year-ago period. Exit activity remained limited, while the period saw the emergence of one new unicorn, space launch company Skyroot Aerospace .
Top 10 deals drive funding
The ten largest funding rounds raised $664 million, accounting for 91 per cent of Telangana's total funding of $726 million in 9M 2026. Hyderabad-based data centre company CtrlS led the list with a $423 million Series B round in June, backed by CPP Investments.
The deal alone accounted for 58 per cent of total funding and 80 per cent of the $527 million increase over 9M 2025.
CtrlS also raised $28.2 million in a Series A round in February, taking its total funding during the period to $451 million.
Skyroot Aerospace raised $60 million in a Series C round in May, while Edubuk secured $50 million in a Series B round in March. Despite the increase in capital raised, Series A and later-stage rounds declined 18 per cent to 23 from 28. The number of first-time funded companies also fell 31 per cent to 20 from 29.
Early-stage funding surged 334 per cent to $622 million from $143 million in 9M 2025, accounting for 86 per cent of the total, said the report.
Advt
The CtrlS Series B round alone contributed 68 per cent of early-stage funding. However, the number of early-stage rounds declined 27 per cent to 19.
According to Trcxn, late-stage funding rose 426 per cent to $78.1 million from $14.8 million, across four rounds compared with two in the year-ago period. However, it remained 84 per cent below the $482 million recorded in 9M 2024. Seed-stage funding declined 35 per cent to $26.4 million, accounting for 4 per cent of the total, while seed-stage rounds fell 35 per cent to 50.
Investor participation also weakened, with the number of active investors declining 22 per cent to 61 from 78. International investors fell 43 per cent to 13 from 23, while first-time investors declined 36 per cent to 30 from 47. AUM Ventures and V3 Ventures made two seed-stage investments each, while Prosus led early-stage investors with two investments in Equal and Deccan AI.
Telangana adds one unicorn
Advt
Acquisitions in Telangana's tech sector declined to six in 9M 2026 from nine in 9M 2025, compared with five in 9M 2024.
IncNut Digital was acquired by Emami for $33.9 million in May 2026, making it the only deal with a disclosed transaction value. The remaining five acquisitions had undisclosed values.
Among the other deals, Perspect was acquired by Unstop, while Alteons Energy was acquired by Sanmar Group, both in September 2026. No acquirer completed more than one deal during the period.
Telangana recorded one public listing in 9M 2026, compared with none in 9M 2025 and one in 9M 2024. Hyderabad-based DSPL went public in January 2026 at a market capitalization of $32.9 million.
Advt
The state also added one unicorn during the period, compared with none in 9M 2025. Hyderabad-based Skyroot Aerospace, which develops launch vehicles for small satellites, achieved unicorn status in May 2026, attaining a valuation of at least $1 billion.
Meanwhile, the number of soonicorns companies identified by Tracxn as potential future unicorns declined 67 per cent to four from 12 in 9M 2025.
